There is no such thing as a strike in the United States. There are labor disputes, and there are lockouts. But there are not strikes because workers have no right to strike under federal law. This was made clear by the Supreme Court case of NLRB v. Mackay Radio & Telegraph Co., 304 U.S. 333 (1938), which said: “A strike does not simply occur when employees cease work; it occurs only when they do so in concerted activities for mutual aid or protection.” That means that workers can’t just quit, they must act together.

There is a very good chance that a Nobel prize would have been awarded to Lise Meitner if she had been born in the right country. The fact is, Meitner was born in Vienna, and that meant that she was German by birth. After Hitler came into power, however, the University of Berlin forced her out. She was then hired at the University of Stockholm. In 1938, when Germany invaded Austria, Meitner fled again to England, where she continued her work. Meitner never received a Nobel prize for her part in discovering nuclear fission because she was Jewish, and therefore could not be honored by Nazi Germany. The Nobel committee later decided to give her an honorary award in 1946.

The term a cappella comes from Italian and literally means in the manner of chapel. The earliest known use of the term is in 1582, when it was used to describe an entire book of sacred music printed without any figured musical notation or tablature whatsoever—only text. For example, one cannot enter into heaven without having accepted Jesus as their personal savior. In some traditions, you must go through a ritual baptism to enter heaven. Tibetan Buddhism flourished in China for centuries, but when the Qing Dynasty fell in 1912, so too did Tibetan influence on Chinese religious life. Still, a significant number of Chinese people practice Tibetan Buddhism today.

The name Hemlock (1843) is not, in fact, a pseudonym for the author, but rather the title of a work by the late John Milton. The work was intended to be an epic poem in which the speaker would travel through time and space as he tells the story of the world's creation. However, the manuscript was lost, and all that remains are some 20 lines of verse that describe the scene where Satan, having just been banished from heaven, falls into a lake of ice and snow. This passage is now considered one of the most moving in English literature, and its few remaining lines have become immensely popular among scholars who believe that the entire work was brilliant.

The word zoonotic is derived from two Greek words, zoon and nosos. Zoon refers to animal or living organism, while nosos means disease. In other words, a zoonotic disease is an infectious disease that can be transmitted between animals and humans. The term originated in 1960s when diseases such as rabies, anthrax, bubonic plague, yellow fever, Lyme disease, avian influenza, Ebola virus disease, HIV/AIDS, and SARS were found to have jumped species barriers.

The word ramshackle is from Middle English, but it has been around for a long time. It can be found in Old French as rammachel and in Old English as hrammelsceal. The word comes from hrammel (the root meaning is unknown) + sceal ("house"). In other words, this was originally an adjective describing a dilapidated house or building. In fact, it was used in the 15th century to mean a dilapidated ship. Nowadays, though, it's more likely to describe something that looks like it will fall apart any minute—and usually with a connotation of being dirty and unkempt.

The word paragon was in use by 1570, according to the Oxford English Dictionary. It comes from French, where it is a diminutive form of par (meaning equal), and originally meant an example or pattern for others to follow. Roughly 35 percent of women ages 18 to 49 are iron deficient, according to new research from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. And while that's lower than the rate for men in this age range (47 percent), it's still cause for concern: Iron is essential for energy production and plays an important role in metabolism. When you don't have enough of it, your body can't make hemoglobin or red blood cells—which means less oxygen will reach your tissues and organs.

Iron is an essential mineral in our bodies. We all need it for many functions including the production of hemoglobin (which carries oxygen), cell growth, immune function, energy production, and brain development. If you are iron deficient, your body cannot perform these tasks optimally and you may experience a range of symptoms from fatigue and weakness to trouble focusing.

And an accompanying picture caption referred imprecisely to the distance from Earth to the planet Proxima b, which orbits one of those stars. The planet is closer than any other known potentially habitable world, but it is more than four times farther from Earth than Venus is.

The mutated form of hemoglobin causes red blood cells to assume a crescent shape instead of the round shape they should be. This makes it harder for them to pass through capillaries and deliver oxygen to organs, causing pain, organ damage, strokes and early death. But some patients also develop severe anemia requiring blood transfusions every few weeks or months.

The word sumptuous, which is a synonym for luxurious and opulent, comes from Latin roots. In fact, it has been used in English since 1620. It is derived from the Latin sumere ("to take"), which itself came from the root sum ("together"). The prefix sup- gives the sense of "over" or "above," so sumptuously can be translated as "taken above."

However, it may be possible to obtain a survivor annuity where monthly payments continue to family members after the death of the annuitant. If you are interested in such an option, contact your financial advisor or benefits administrator.

The other meaning of ordeal is for a form of criminal punishment, based on the belief that someone who was guilty would be injured by touching hot iron or fire. This use of ordeal is usually found only in historical writing.

At Kentucky Fried Chicken, the fried chicken is soaked in a brine solution that contains 20% salt by weight. The company then washes off most of the excess salt and packs its fried chicken in plastic bags to keep it moist and fresh. But after about four days, the remaining salt will start to draw water out of the chicken meat, making it less juicy and more dry and tough. So KFC keeps its fried chicken in a refrigerator at temperatures just above freezing—a process called cryopreservation—to slow down the evaporation of moisture from the chicken.

Of the many important contributions to Southern Studies over the past decade, perhaps none has been more significant than the growing attention to art and culture. As I argue in this article, a number of scholars have begun to rethink Southern history by including cultural analysis into their work. In so doing, they are recovering an artistic tradition that was once dismissed as provincial or insignificant. In addition to addressing these recent developments, my essay also provides a brief overview of how this field emerged, starting with the work of Richard Hofstadter and then moving through several key works by William Ferris, Thomas Holt, and David Roediger. Finally, I offer some concluding thoughts on why the study of Southern visual arts is so important.

The word allusive is derived from a Latin term that means "to be evasive." Today, this word refers to something that has many indirect references. It also can mean something that is subtle or vague. You might say a movie was allusive if it had a lot of hints about what was going on but didn't give away too much information. This is a very specific type of hinting. For example, you could say the movie was alluding to the fact that the main character would die at the end, without ever saying so directly.

Forcing bulbs is a fun way to bring color into your home at the darkest time of year. Forcing involves using warm temperatures and light to trick the plants into thinking it's springtime, so they will bloom early in response. This can be done with amaryllis, paperwhite narcissus, hyacinth, tulips or crocus. Choose bulbs that are large enough for forcing. Smaller bulbs won't have enough energy stored up to bloom on schedule. You don't need to force bulbs that grow naturally during this season; you can just plant them outdoors as usual when the weather warms up.

When someone behaves in this way it's easy to feel like you have something to prove, but if you let your emotions get the better of you then you might also start acting in an arrogant manner. The word desalination is derived from a combination of the prefix de- and the root salinity, which means saltiness. The prefix de- means "not," so we can think of desalination as not being salty or the removal of salt. Desalination is commonly used in water purification, but it can also refer to the process of removing salt from other substances like foods. The word desalinate has been around since 1957, but desalinization has been around since at least 1846.

When I go back and look at my journals from the 1970s, it is clear that I was obsessed with semicolons. The semicolon was a symbol of rebellion for me, but not in any way connected to politics or social movements; rather, it was a symbol of self-determination in a personal sense. “A wild petal flies from the thicket,” wrote William Blake, “To the summer air.” Or so he thought. In truth, the petal was in his head. It was one of the many visions that he saw all through his life and recorded in verse and images with unparalleled energy and imagination. They were published as engravings or woodcuts in books like Songs of Innocence (1789), Songs of Experience (1794) and Jerusalem: The Emanation of the Giant Albion (1804–20). Blake was an artist, poet and prophet who believed that God spoke to him and inspired his work. He also believed that his prints could help transform society by bringing people closer to God.

The word dhow is a noun, and it has several meanings. One meaning is a traditional sailing vessel that originated in India and Iran and is still used today on rivers and coasts in South Asia. A second meaning is a type of sailing ship with one or more masts with lateen sails that was traditionally used along the east coast of Africa to transport goods between East African ports and the Persian Gulf countries. A third meaning is a wooden ship with one or two masts that was once widely used throughout Southeast Asia as a trading and fishing boat. Dhows were also used for pirate attacks and by smugglers. The word comes from the Arabic term ra's, which means planked ship or boat made of wood.

Silhouettes of patrolling falcons, kites and eagles were common sights at the world’s major airports during World War II. The word portentous is a great example of how words can evolve in meaning over time. Portentous comes from the Latin word portentum, which means “omen.” In ancient Rome, an omen was any kind of sign that foretold future events. The word was used to describe both good and bad signs—for instance, the Romans believed that when birds flew in large groups it was a positive omen. But if the birds were ravens or crows, the omen was negative.

The word kvetch (pronounced KVECH) has a number of different meanings, depending on how you use it. It can be used as an adjective or a noun, and it refers to the act of complaining, especially about small, insignificant things. If someone is kvetching, they are complaining about something, but if something is kvetchy, then it means that it’s annoying in some way. The word also relates to other languages, such as the Hebrew word kvetshn, which means “to complain,” so you might want to learn a few words in another language just for fun!

The International Court of Justice, known as the World Court, is the United Nations’ judicial branch. The court was established in 1945 by the U.N.’s Charter and began its work in 1946. It is the successor to the Permanent Court of International Justice (PCIJ), which was created under the League of Nations after World War I but never had a permanent home. The ICJ is based in The Hague in the Netherlands, where it has been located since 1986. Its seat is called the Peace Palace because it was built for the PCIJ and dedicated with those words from John Haynes Holmes in 1913.

When it comes to investing, you need to understand the difference between wealth and net worth. Net worth is simply your assets minus liabilities (what you own minus what you owe). It's a snapshot of your finances in time. But wealth is something very different: It's a measure of how much money you have on hand that can be converted into cash without having to sell assets at distressed prices or take out loans. In other words, bookshelf wealth is a measure of how much cash you can lay your hands on right now — the stuff you could go buy if you wanted to. As Justice Scalia has said, “It is easy to overstate how important a case is.” The Supreme Court’s job is to settle cases and controversies between states or between a state and citizens of another state. It does this by deciding whether it will hear appeals from lower courts. This decision is called granting certiorari. If the court grants certiorari, the justices then decide which side they agree with and why. The justices write opinions in which they explain their reasoning. These explanations can be very long or very short; sometimes only a few words suffice. Sometimes there are several concurring or dissenting opinions written by one or more justices.

The word kowtow is a verb that means to show obedience or respect by bowing with one’s head touching the ground. The word derives from the Chinese term gōutuow, which means “to kneel on both knees,” but it is usually used in English as a noun referring to the act of bowing. Kowtow entered English in 1790 via the French form couteau, and was first recorded in the 1832 work A Glossary of Provincial Words Used In the Counties of Somerset, Dorset, Devon, Cornwall, and the Isle of Man by Robert Southey (1774-1843).

A somewhat obscure but useful concept in NLP is that of "anchoring." It's a term that means something different depending on what part of NLP you're talking about. In the field of hypnosis, it refers to associating an internal state with a trigger such as a word or gesture. Whenever the trigger is used, the person will go into trance. In the world of cognitive therapy and positive psychology, anchors are things people can do to change their mood or outlook. They are often used to anchor positive emotions, but they can be used for any emotion. For example, some people put their hand over their heart when they remember someone they love who has passed away.

The word klaxon is a blend of two words, klaxon horn and alarm. The term was coined in 1907 by American inventor J.W. Wade, who had just patented his new kind of automobile horn. He chose to name it after the Greek goddess Klaxos, which means “sound” or “noise.” (Klaxos was one of Apollo’s many love interests.) By 1908, the word klaxon had appeared in print for the first time—in an advertisement for the new invention. From there it spread rapidly through English-speaking countries around the world. Today, it can be found everywhere from dictionaries to computer games to the dictionary of slang expressions.

The word proportionate was first used by Aristotle. It is a Latin word that means to share in common, or having parts in equal shares. In math, it means dividing into parts so that each part has an equal relationship to the whole. A good example would be when we cut pizza into four equal slices for our family. When we are talking about war and peace, it can mean how the loss of life and destruction caused by a conflict is shared among all parties involved. The word proportionate is also often used as a synonym for fair. We'll use that in a moment.
